answer_text: A REST API is a web API that follows REST architectural constraints: stateless, client-server, cacheable, uniform interface. Resources are identified by URIs. HTTP methods map to CRUD operations: GET retrieves, POST creates, PUT updates, DELETE removes. It returns JSON or XML. GraphQL differs in that you specify exactly what fields you need in a single query, reducing over-fetching.
notes: Accurate REST definition; correctly distinguishes GraphQL

answer_text: SQL indexes speed up SELECT queries by creating a separate data structure the database can scan instead of doing a full table scan. B-tree indexes are the default in most databases. You'd add an index on columns used frequently in WHERE clauses or JOINs. Trade-off: indexes slow down INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE because the index must also be updated. For a table with millions of rows, a composite index on (user_id, created_at) can reduce query time from seconds to milliseconds.
notes: Excellent SQL index answer; covers B-tree, trade-offs, composite index example

answer_text: Machine learning models learn statistical patterns from training data. Supervised learning uses labeled data to learn mappings from input to output — for example, logistic regression for classification or random forests for non-linear boundaries. The bias-variance tradeoff is central: a high-capacity model (like deep neural networks) can overfit, so we regularize with dropout, L2, or reduce model complexity. I've trained gradient boosting models with XGBoost for fraud detection, reducing false positives by 22%.
notes: Excellent; covers bias-variance, regularization, real production experience

answer_text: A load balancer distributes incoming traffic across multiple backend servers to prevent any single server from becoming a bottleneck. Common algorithms include round-robin, least-connections, and IP hash (for session affinity). Layer 4 load balancers work at the TCP level; Layer 7 (like AWS ALB or Nginx) can route based on HTTP content like path or hostname. I used Nginx with upstream servers and health checks in our staging environment.
notes: Strong; covers algorithms, L4/L7 distinction, real usage

answer_text: SOLID stands for Single Responsibility, Open-Closed, Liskov Substitution, Interface Segregation, Dependency Inversion. Single Responsibility means a class should have one reason to change. Open-Closed means open for extension, closed for modification. Dependency Inversion means high-level modules shouldn't depend on low-level modules; both should depend on abstractions. I apply these daily: for example, I use interfaces and dependency injection in my Spring Boot services.
notes: All 5 principles named; 3 explained with detail; practical application cited
